Summarize the population coefficients of a fitted joint cluster model

Source: R/joint-analysis.R
catmech_joint_summary.Rd

Summarizes the true-measurement fixed effects from every retained posterior draw, on the original response and predictor scales. These are model-based Bayesian credible intervals, conditional on the joint model and its priors. They are not cluster-robust confidence intervals or summaries of a different downstream analysis.

Usage

catmech_joint_summary(result, level = 0.95)

Arguments

result

A result from [catmech_reference()] with `cluster_model = "joint"` and a fitted, converged posterior. The all-reference shortcut has no parameter posterior and is refused without refitting.

level

Central posterior credible interval probability, strictly between zero and one.

Value

A data frame with one row per original design coefficient: `term`, posterior mean `estimate`, `posterior_sd`, `lower`, `upper`, `level`, `rhat`, `ess_bulk`, `ess_tail`, `mcse_mean`, `mcse_lower`, `mcse_upper`, `draws`, `iterations`, `chains`, and `interpretation`.

Details

The estimand is the population fixed-effect vector for the true measurement in the original imputation design. Under the model's zero-mean random effects independent of the covariates, these coefficients describe the marginal mean of the true measurement as well as the mean conditional on a zero site effect. They are not the least-squares coefficients of the realized completed cohort. The function has no formula argument: it cannot change predictors, add an offset or interaction, or use the repaired measurement as a predictor.

All retained iterations from all chains are used, independently of the number of completed datasets. The mean, sample standard deviation and equal-tailed quantiles (R quantile type 7) summarize those draws. There is no additional Rubin pooling, cluster sandwich variance, or Student t multiplier.

Fixed effects are transformed jointly, including the contribution of predictor centering to the original-scale intercept. Rank-normalized R-hat and bulk and tail effective sample sizes are recomputed for these coefficients. R-hat must be at most 1.05 and both effective sample sizes at least `100 * chains`. Failure raises a `catmech_convergence_error` carrying `model_diagnostics` for the transformed coefficient draws. The `posterior` package supplies Monte Carlo errors for the mean and interval endpoints. These quantify simulation error, not uncertainty about model adequacy or the population coefficient. Passing diagnostics does not establish frequentist interval coverage.
